title: SciTeX doctor report, spec_version 1
description: A package's checks rolled up into one verdict. FOUR KEYS, and the rolled-up `ok` is three-valued exactly as a check's is. WHAT AN UNKNOWN MEANS FOR THE ROLLUP IS THE CALLER'S DECISION and is NOT carried here: `refuse` (an unknown blocks — never act on a host you could not inspect), `propagate` (the rollup is itself unknown) and `tolerate` (an unknown does not block) are all legal, so a reader MUST NOT infer from a top-level `ok: true` that every check was answered. `summary` is where that is visible: it NAMES every unknown check, under every policy. See verdicts.yaml.

package.description: Which package this doctor speaks for.

ok.description: The rolled-up verdict, three-valued. A known failure anywhere makes this false under every policy. null appears only under the `propagate` policy, and means the rollup itself could not be established.

checks.description: The individual answers, in the order they were asked.

summary.description: Counts, then the names of the failing checks, then the names of the UNKNOWN ones. The unknowns are named under every policy — a tolerated unknown is still an unknown, and an aggregate that answers `ok` without saying what it could not see has lied by omission.

unknown_policy.description: FORBIDDEN on the wire. It is a property of the CALLER's decision rather than of the observation, and adding a fifth key would make every existing reader of this four-key record wrong about a shape that was not the problem. Read the unknowns from `summary`.
